title: I see games being made in three.js using AI that look almost as good as games done in UE5.
author: FutureLynx_
selftext:
Is UE5 cooked? Who will want to install 80 GB engine, that takes time to kick off, and takes time to compile, when you can make a game and small little engine super customized to the needs of your game using AI and three.js or other simpler framework? Add in to the equation that games are being cloned in hours...

I think this is why they are coping and stopped at UE5.8. It will be soon a dinossaur.

I have been working everyday with Unreal for a few years, and the engine always felt wrong to me because of friction. At the same time i loved a lot of things about it, and learned a lot with it. But i remember many times thinking about just moving to Godot or even JS and make a simpler 2D game.

I made some posts complaining about Blueprints years ago. Especially how they interact with C++ and how awful they are to maintain, without even mentioning they are not good with AI. 

I also posted about what if epic removed Blueprints from the engine...

My posts were often downvoted, and everyone in the comments saying Blueprints will never be removed. It turns out my intuition was right, and they announced some months ago that Blueprints will be removed.

Now I dont know what they are cooking for UE6, but I imagine it will be yet another super bloated tool. 

I hope not. I hope Unreal makes something ergonomic, more minimalistic and straightforward. Because we need good engines and alternatives. But I'm afraid that it will be a disaster and finally make a lot of people leave for Godot or Unity.

They will remove blueprints which is something that I welcome, but blueprints is what is keeping the old users in Unreal, because they like blueprints and invested a lot of time learning it. While not making the engine any better in terms of speed, performance and ergonomics, most probably worse in all these 3 + adding a bunch of tools to make it even more bloated.

Godot opens super fast, it is pleasant to work with. I think Unreal is about to get cooked any day.

comments.author: tonios2
comments.body:
The performance and capabilities of a native game engine are far better than browser + three.js, browser was not built for game engines, all the algorithms ..etc need to be built using JS, and the graphics API only provides pieces of what real native drivers provide.  
  
Not that three.js tech demos can't look nice, but if you want to make a real game, just use a native graphics library or some game engine.
